subject: Region pinning exception & temporary egress window — DPA addendum request
messages:
From: Lucy Brennan <dpo@medica.co.uk>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medica.co.uk>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions for DPA addendum — region pin + transient egress window

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the overview during yesterday's call. We're moving past initial security review and need a narrow set of commitments to close procurement: specifically, (1) a binding statement of region pinning for EU-hosted workloads (data and model inference) and (2) clear, written limits on any temporary cross-border processing for failover, analytics, or backups.

Our DPO has asked for a proposed clause that limits transient cross-border processing to a defined maximum window, plus an operational notification requirement (who to notify and timeline). Can Redwood confirm:
- Whether region pinning can be contractually guaranteed for our EU production workspace?
- If failover or analytics ever require processing outside EU, what is the maximum duration Redwood expects, and will you provide notification in advance (or as soon as practical)?

We attached a short list of DPA questions and the template clause we tried to use with another vendor. Happy to review edits to the clause.

Regards,
Lucy Brennan
DPO, Medica Health
Attachment: medica_dpa_questions.docx
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Brennan <dpo@medica.co.uk>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions for DPA addendum — region pin + transient egress window

Hi Lucy — thank you, and appreciated the clear asks. I looped in Marissa (Legal) and Kimberly (Ops) to make sure we propose language that aligns with our operational guarantees. High level answers:

- Region pinning: yes — we can provide an EU-region pining addendum for your production workspace that restricts placement and primary inference processing to EU regions. That will be codified in the DPA addendum and the service config.

- Temporary cross-border processing: we operate a small set of transient failover behaviors (e.g., disaster recovery, autoscaling bursts to alternative capacity, and non-production analytics). For production inference paths we aim to avoid any egress; if an exceptional temporary hop is required, we can commit to notification and a maximum window.

Marissa — could you propose specific contractual language (max window + notification SLAs)? Kimberly — can you confirm typical operational windows for failover and whether we can limit to X hours in the addendum?

Next steps: we'll draft a short addendum and share a proposed clause + subprocessor roster. If that looks good to Medica, we can route to DocuSign and Procurement.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-23T08:27:00Z
Subject: RE: Questions for DPA addendum — region pin + transient egress window

Rachel / Marissa — quick ops context to feed the legal clause:

1) Production inference: We can pin Medica's production workspace to EU primary region(s) and ensure inference-serving instances are drawn from EU capacity pools. That covers the primary request.

2) Transient cross-border processing scenarios we observe:
   - Disaster recovery failover (multi-region switchover) — happens only upon region-level outage and requires orchestration of capacity allocation.
   - Short autoscale bursting when EU capacity is temporarily constrained and customer has agreed to burst to equivalent-performance capacity (rare; usually involves reserved capacity options).
   - Asynchronous analytics and non-prod telemetry that runs in a central analytics cluster (we can exclude/bind this for Medica).

3) Suggested operational commitments we can offer for the addendum:
   - Notification: Redwood will notify the customer security contact and DPO within 48 hours of any non-routine cross-border processing event that impacts production data.
   - Maximum transient window: For DR-driven failovers and emergency bursts, Redwood will limit temporary processing outside EU to a maximum of 72 hours unless mutually agreed in writing for an extension.
   - Scope restriction: We will exclude non-production analytics and telemetry from the production pin by default and provide a roster of subprocessors.

Technical caveat: Some edge cache nodes and ephemeral KV caching used to accelerate token inference may replicate small prefixes across nearby regions for latency optimization; we can disable that behavior for pinned workspaces (with SLA trade-offs).

Jordan — please add any routing/policy knobs we should make configurable in the customer console so Medica can control burst behavior.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Brennan <dpo@medica.co.uk>, Procurement Team <procurement@medica.co.uk>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T15:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions for DPA addendum — region pin + transient egress window

Hi Lucy / Procurement team — following up with the confirmed proposal from Redwood: attached is a one-page DPA addendum draft and our current subprocessor roster. Key points captured:

- EU region pinning for Medica production workspace: Redwood will ensure primary inference processing and model-serving instances are placed in EU regions only.
- Transient cross-border processing: Redwood may perform temporary cross-border processing for classified exceptional events (DR failover, emergency capacity burst). Redwood will:
    * Notify Medica's DPO and security contact within 48 hours of any such event (operational and timeline details in notification).
    * Limit any temporary processing outside the EU to a maximum of 72 hours unless both parties agree to a written extension.
- Edge cache behavior: we will disable ephemeral cross-region prefix caching for the pinned workspace unless you explicitly enable it.

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_Medica_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster.csv

Next steps: If the language looks acceptable, we will: (1) have Marissa finalize minor edits, (2) share the DocuSign link for signature, and (3) schedule a short ops call (15 min) to review console controls for pinning and burst policies. Proposed HubSpot deal: 67890.

I'll await your confirmation and any redline suggestions.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA_Addendum_Medica_v1.pdf; subprocessor_roster.csv
